walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Investigative Study — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Investigative Study brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Investigative Study.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose Seven Dimensions framework analyses religion?
options: Eliade
Smart
Otto
Wach
Weber
Durkheim
Frazer
Tylor
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.

mcqs.q: What is the Eightfold Path in Buddhism?
options: The practical path to ending suffering: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline.
The Eightfold Path is the same as the Four Noble Truths.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
